a.text: You're hurt.
Am I? That new Arts teacher is so scary. Maybe I got bruised by him during training earlier.
It hurts.
Does it? It's nothing. The Arts in our bodies will heal our wounds in no time.
Hm... Why are you crying, Hildegard? Haven't you been injured far worse than this before?
No, we can't.... we shouldn't be treated like this.
Hand me the wooden sword. I'll go look for that caster.
I'll go find Leopold and everyone who treats us like creations instead of recognizing us as people with feelings.
And what are you going to do after that?
Resist.
You might not even achieve anything.
That's fine. I just need to prove something to them all, to you, and to myself.
Which is?
That I'm alive. And that my sorrow, my joy, my pain, my love, and my life... that they definitely mean something.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: It's beautiful... just like it always has been.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: It's getting colder lately. Autumn will be over in a month or two. But Zwillingstürme doesn't tend to see any snow, so the sunset won't wane.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: This is surreal. You're definitely not the type to soliloquize while appreciating the view.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: What I'm trying to say is that there are no longer any traces of unrest, after just half a month.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The Twin Spires tower over us as usual, the clouds are as splendid as always, and the people pass by both Gnade Avenue and Macht Avenue as if... nothing happened at all.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: No, something has changed. We can't ignore that.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: How are your injuries?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The old man said it's nothing serious, but you did stay in Kargereich for a bit too long, so it's hard to say if you're completely free of corrosion.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I haven't had any more headaches since then, at least.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You're braver than I imagined, Ebenholz. You've saved so many people.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I just... couldn't allow those 'echoes' haunting me to hurt any more people.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You met the Witch King, and whether you cursed or killed him, you've already completed 'the last thing you could still do.'

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: So what's next for you?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I hope I'm not intruding on you both.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Herr Ebenholz, I was looking for you... on Grimmacht's behalf.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And here I thought it would be Ewigegnade to send you to punish a 'dead man' for coming back to Leithanien without permission.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What's this?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Grimmacht handed me two secret letters.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: One calling for your return to Zwillingstürme, and the other granting you a final choice.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Have you been staying in the spire the whole time since the incident?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Officially, there are still two Kaiserinnen in Leithanien. Grimmacht is just away for the time being, and someone has to handle the mountain of paperwork she left behind.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Only I can do it, as I always have.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You're set on that?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Leithanien might have only one single Spire in the future.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I came to Zwillingstürme to meet with the Kaiserinnen seven years ago. Ewigegnade didn't like my performance, my caution, or maybe my status as Lupukarn's representative... It was Grimmacht who saved me.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: And it didn't end there. I am her Voice, even if she didn't, and now never will, appoint me as one for real.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: You, me, and even some of the nobility—many Leithanians believe in the path Grimmacht was seeking, right?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: It might lead us to an era where we won't need Spires at all. There's still so much more we can do.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The way you're talking...

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You've matured since the last time I saw you, Michael.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Erm, that's because... I'm a growing boy, after all.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Herr Ebenholz, I see you're done reading the letters, so I'll take my leave now.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Whatever your answer is, I hope you'll be happy with it.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Your expression is a little hard to read.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Grimmacht gave me two options.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I could get another death certificate. Not just as 'Graf Urtica,' but also as a 'Leithanian'... By dying, I will obtain true freedom.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Or... I could return to the Urtica Grafschaft.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Let me tell you a story.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: There was once a young boy...

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: I'm not very good at telling stories, but just listen to me.

The boy's family served as retainers to a certain aristocracy for generations. From one generation to the next, the retainers fought on the nobles' behalf, shedding blood, vying for glory, and bearing any rebukes for them.
Until a certain noble came along. Birth, tradition, systems... He saw them all as worthless. Everyone looked the same to him: mediocre, frail, and shallow.
So with a piece of paper, he removed the status of every retainer working for his family, and the boy's family obtained their freedom.

Afterwards, the noble became the most controversial ruler in the history of the country. His crimes eventually eclipsed his accomplishments, his Spire was toppled, and the empire ushered in a new age.
Many decisions made during his lifetime were also overruled, including the decree to remove his retainers' shackles.

One day, the young boy was told that the deposed king's descendant was granted leniency by the new Kaiser, and had regained his family's territory. He was told he needed to rush back to the spire, to meet his master...
Fate seemed to only turn a corner before coming right back again.

But in the end, the boy never managed to enter the spire. The newly arrived noble refused to sign the documents that could get him his servant back. This new noble, as they said, was also a boy around his age...
Once again, the boy obtained 'freedom.'

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The boy's name was Lessing Maeyer. And that newly arrived noble was you, Ebenholz, the twelve year old Graf Urtica.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You'll never remember it, so don't bother trying.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Back then I was so full of anxiety, afraid that someone was playing a prank on me, so I asked a servant to find out what was going on.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: She said: 'The young Graf's migraines seem to be upsetting him again. He chased all the attendants out of his room, with many documents scattered across the floor.'

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Don't take this as grumbling about some 'fateful arrangement.' I'm just telling the truth about how one unintentional move from you changed someone else's entire life.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You spurned your identity, as well as the regrets and suffering you bore from it. Of course, I'm sure you know better than anyone else how real your pain was.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: But at the same time, I hope you also know their value.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: And how we should regard them.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Danke, for telling me all this, even though you were positively awful at it.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Have I ever mentioned what I experienced back at the Genesis Horn?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Nein.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I didn't think it worth bringing up before, but I suppose I can tell you what I didn't get to tell the Witch King, before he vanished in front of my eyes.
You have no heir. I'm merely a descendant who shares the name Urtica.
Before your time, it had yet to carry either honor or so-called disgrace.
This changed because of you alone. So I will change it once more, but never by the same means you used.
This is my way of mocking you.
This is my shame, my cage.
This is my duty, my obligation.
This is my path.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: So you had already decided back then?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Then why did you make that face earlier, while you were reading the Kaiserin's letters?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Because there are still other matters, which have suddenly became somewhat tricky to deal with.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Ebenholz!!!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I finally found you!!!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hibiscus...?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Have you forgotten who you are?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You're a Rhodes Island Operator. I'm sure you've read the operator manual you got after onboarding, right? Carefully, from cover to cover?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: 'I invite all of you to witness how two centuries of sin will come to a conclusion... How fortunate it is, that this day of farewell has finally arrived! ...For I have seen my life's path ahead of me, crystal clear...'

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: What's that she reading?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Operators must go through a strict approval process whenever they apply to leave the landship. How could you just run off after leaving that unintelligible letter?

spans.text: go through a strict approval process whenever they apply to leave the landship. How could you just run off after leaving that unintelligible letter?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I haven't even had time to hand it in yet.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...Give it back, Hibiscus.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'll be staying in Leithanien for the foreseeable future. I'll return to the Urtica Grafschaft.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: As I'd like to resubmit my application to disembark, could you please help me to—

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Erm, you'd better go see the Doctor or Kal'tsit in person for that.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Is the landship nearby?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: How else would I be here? It's not that close, but we do have some business nearby to handle.

spans.text: How else would I be here? It's not
close, but we do have some business nearby to handle.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You don't seem at all surprised to hear that I want to return to Urtica. We've been on edge ever since we left Vyseheim...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: That's because you weren't gnashing your teeth spouting nonsense this time. Which means you've thought this through.
Zwillingstürme, Bachshof, Bach Street
Viviana looks at the courtyard before her.

It is not large by any measure, but still well maintained. The low stone steps surrounding the planted vegetation have been removed and enclosed with a waxy white oak fence, presumably to prevent the homeowners from tripping over them.
A small house sits quietly in the center, embraced by the grass. Freshly painted white walls reflect the morning sun, casting the climbing vines in a radiant glow.
Come in, Viviana.
You made it.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: When Bach was presiding over the Glorreiches Kapitalprojekt, he specially patterned this street after the one he lived in as a child. Doesn't it bear a striking resemblance to Marigold Alley?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Two years ago, a Markgraf returned to their territory to recuperate from illness, so Cora bought this place, but never moved in.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: It was only after you came to the city that she asked me to come help clean the place up.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: So, how does it look?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It's lovely. Only... these vines don't have to be trimmed so much.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Let them grow as they please, or they'll look somewhat stiff.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...There's no need to hold back your thoughts, Viviana.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Herr Reiner, this is the first time I'm seeing your face.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: It's been so many years.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: This is the first time I've taken off the Gesatzswächter mask and shown my true face to anyone else, not since I came to Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: It's my identity, my duty, and... my everything.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: I guess a Gesatzswächter shouldn't be reminiscing about the mastermind who spoiled Das Kaiserinnensfest and tampered with the Güldenesgesatz.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Herr Reiner, about what happened that day...

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: There's no need to blame yourself, Viviana.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: Whenever Cora set her heart on something, she would never look back. You could only be dragged along with her.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: Her eyes were already going when she joined the Reichsorchester on Werner's recommendation that year. I promised Werner I'd do my best to help the girl he saved.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: But I gradually came to discover that she had her own feelings, her own judgements, her own desires.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: She wanted to help Lucinda, to save Werner, and even to modify the Güldenesgesatz. She wanted to ensure that the kindhearted people would never be tormented by their own regrets ever again.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: She was... a resolute woman, and I've always respected her.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: But she was even more courageous than I had thought.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Mhm...

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: And so, her fate is sealed.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: If it were me...

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: I... I can't even imagine how it would feel.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: ...Thank you, Viviana.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: Have you made your decision?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I went to see Ewigegnade before coming here, and formally declined her offer to become an Empresses' Voice.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: As per protocol, new recruits have to enter the Spires after the Celebration and accept Their Majesties' appointment before they can officially assume their positions.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But Her Majesty Grimmacht has just 'lost her voice,' and this year's appointment ceremony has been cancelled, so it's an appropriate time to submit my refusal.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: If this is what you've decided on, then I have nothing to say.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: It's just that, Werner...

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: Viviana, this was the best, and last, thing he could arrange for you.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: Don't blame your father. He just lacked the freedom to do otherwise.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: My father... let me and my mother down, but he protected so many others.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Cora in the Witch King's Spire, House Hochberg which could have been implicated at any moment, and the countless people of Sturmland forced into a difficult position by a copy of the Güldenesgesatz.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: From beginning to end, he was caught up in the vortex of his time. He witnessed, experienced, lost, was powerless to change anything, and could only do his utmost to fend off the storm.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: He never left a single line, but regardless, this is a poet's way of writing about himself.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: Viviana...

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: I'm glad you feel that way, child.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Whether sending me to Kazimierz or arranging my appointment as an Empresses' Voice, it was never because he thought the paths he chose for me were good.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: He simply saw me as a child in need of constant protection, a job at which he failed to excel.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So I don't blame him.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: Then I presume you won't be returning to Sturmland either.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: In Kazimierz, I felt like a stranger. The bright neon lights, the noisy arenas, the priced battles, as well as the glory and honor... they were never a part of me.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But when I returned to Sturmland, to Zwillingstürme, that feeling never went away.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: To me, Leithanien is just the candles and books I had back in those dark nights. The marigolds in bloom everywhere. They also symbolize 'parting.'

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I've always been able to make my own choices.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: ...Choices.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: People can only truly face their own weaknesses when they have options.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Herr Reiner...

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: It's nothing.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: After Das Kaiserinnensfest, you said you needed to inform your friends in Kazimierz about your experience in Kargereich.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I've already sent a letter. I should be receiving a reply soon.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: And after that?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: 'To the lighthouses. To where once they were.'

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Just a line from a book I read when I was young.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Allow me to bid you farewell. Lebewohl, Herr Reiner.

steps.name: Brandt
steps.text: Lebewohl.

a.text: Goodbye, Cora.
Goodbye, Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: Frau Droste! Phew—

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: Frau Droste, the 'Nearl' you've been waiting two weeks for is finally here. Just up ahead at the crossing.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Madam Viviana Droste.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Mr. Młynar...

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: The Nearl family has received your correspondence. I just happened to be near Leithanien, so I came as soon as I could.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: In your letter, you mentioned seeing, and even touching, a campaign knight's swordspear with the Nearl family crest.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Tell me everything.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: So, this is the melody of the present moment?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What you're hearing are all the emotions I'm feeling.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: ...It's no different from what I usually hear.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The people of Zwillingstürme love you, after all.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And you love them too.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: This has never changed.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You were there too, when I returned to reality from the Genesis Horn.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Perform the melody back then for me, Sankta.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: That's impossible.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I cannot record the moment the tear rolled down your cheek. If it did not fall into the depths of your soul to bloom into fruition, then it was merely a drop of water impossible to retain, evaporated by the sun as it fell.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: The year this spire was built, a scholar gave a public lecture at the Leithanian Academy of Arts. He claimed that people born from Arts lack an innate soul.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: The very next day, he received... a transfer, a promotion normally impossible for him to obtain in his lifetime: becoming the Kaiserin's attendant.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Unfortunately, he passed just a year later from overworking himself in the depths of the spire. Though he left behind a scholarly magnum opus before his death, overturning all of his previous opinions.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Would you like to have a look at it, Sankta? The writing is mediocre, so I did not allow its publication. But the emotions contained within are... actually quite interesting.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Are you... planning to lock me up in your spire, too?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Who let you in, Sankta?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: The Kaiserin has not approved your audience!

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Bring him over.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Executor Federico of the Laterano Notarial Hall. I have recently submitted several requests to the Empresses' Voices for an audience.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: So you're... the Lateran Saint.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am here to recover the fugitive Arturia.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Your sister has done many things in Leithanien.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Former Reichsorchester Tuner Cora Löwenstein and the remnants of the Witch King—

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: ...Cora? No, I'm not talking about that.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: The Ludwigs-Universität case concluded long ago. Das Kaiserinnensfest did go through some incidents, but the final performance was satisfactory.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: I'm sure you've seen the whole thing, Herr Saint. I hope Leithanien's might and magnificence will leave a deep impression on you, even after you leave.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Am I to take your statement as such: 'Leithanien is prepared to refuse any procedural communication with Laterano over Arturia and her criminal offences'?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Are you questioning my decision?
Federico hears the sound of swords and floor colliding.
He lifts his head and looks at the Empress of Leithanien.
Ewigegnade stands in the sunset's afterglow, her long skirt infused with a warm gold. But behind her lies a long hallway comprised of shadows.
He counts dozens of Gesatzswächter standing at attention in silence, their swords resounding.
Federico Giallo. Don't move just yet.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: And what is this? An Arts device... A Lateran made drone?

steps.name: 'Unique Drone Model'
steps.text: I'm just a little machine.

steps.name: 'Unique Drone Model'
steps.text: On some occasions, you can also treat me as a Messenger.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: And to whom do you belong?

steps.name: 'Unique Drone Model'
steps.text: I belong to... Laterano.

steps.name: 'Unique Drone Model'
steps.text: There is someone who wishes to speak with you, Empress of Leithanien.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Long time no see, Ewigegnade.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: ...Your Holiness.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Your Majesty, Arturia Giallo has been taken away.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Yes, I saw.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: If you wish to keep her here, then we shall not let them leave so easily, even if Yvangelista XI himself were to show up in person.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Of course you wouldn't.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: However, that aging Pope has brought us a message.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: He said that... 'Disaster' is imminent. And when the time comes, Laterano won't be the only nation affected. He hopes for Leithanien and Laterano to cooperate and overcome this crisis together.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: His usual rhetoric then.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Herkunftshorn said something similar.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Within the chaos, right before the illusory throne he had created for himself.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: He said, 'hope is already lost, and eternity is no more'.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: And then, after that, I saw them with my own eyes... The enemy hibernating within the chaos.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: At one point, they came infinitesimally close to our Leithanien.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...Give us the order, and we will bring the Sankta back for you.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: No, not just her. We will do anything, no matter the cost... Whatever it takes to find a way to re-enter that chaotic space and bring Grimmacht back.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Hildegard...

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: In the final moment before the Genesis Horn completely disintegrated, I raised my shield, protecting the twin spires and everyone beneath... but not her.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...What?!

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Brandt, watch this sunset with me.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: I asked her if she wanted to know why.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: If she wanted to ask why I let everything be, even though I knew it would turn out as it did.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Or to ask me why... I turned my back on her at the very last moment.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: But she didn't.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: She didn't even hesitate to do what she normally does, turning to face the enemy head on.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: As we passed each other, her final words were to wish that...

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: ...I could have this sunset, as I wanted.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Grimmacht... is a great ruler.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: We will never forget her sacrifice, and continue the fight for Leithanien's future.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: So you've made your decision too.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...Yes, Your Majesty.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Very good, Brandt.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Herkunftshorn built a spire in that impossible chaos, naming it after the tower that has long since crumbled in reality.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: He declared that it would stand eternal.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Therefore, I can achieve the same. No, I can surpass it, even.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: I will keep this sunset for all eternity.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: It will bathe Leithanien, and everything that will belong to Leithanien, in Eternal Grace.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: That's the last of it. It's not like you'll be able to stuff the spire down your pocket if you keep staring at it, you know!

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: ...But is that truly impossible?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Professor!

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Alright, alright, don't glare at me like that. I'll return the statue I got from the Beschwörung classroom's entrance, if it comes down to it.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: You put that thing in my cube-thing?!

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: What? It's valuable, you know. I spilled Feranmut blood all over it a century ago!

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Let's... get a move on. The rest of us are going, even if you aren't.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Ermengarde, are we really...

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: There's no way a Lich can become a Leithanian. Shouldn't you know that better than anyone else, having been here the longest?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: The Sarkaz have always wandered this land, and us Liches have always been the nomads of our people.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: We walk the land collecting and guarding knowledge. We protect our tradition from war and strife, so we leave the moment the place we're at isn't stable anymore.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: And Leithanien's about to undergo some radical changes. Grimmacht stayed behind in the chaos, so there's no one left to hold Ewigegnade back.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Heh... Herkunftshorn, you damn codger. You ought to die a thousand more deaths for the mess you've left us. Feel like coming back to life again and wipe your own behind?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: An impossible feat even if you were to say yes. And if such an opportunity did exist, we should leave it to the more sprightly youngsters anyway.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Do you mean there's a chance for Grimmacht to... Have you come up with a way to enter Kargereich?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Easy now, it won't happen so soon.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: But Herkunftshorn was right. The time of annihilation is nigh.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Where will us Liches find our place when the entire land is beset by calamity?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: And that's why we shouldn't bother ourselves with all that trouble. Our nomad days shall come to an end.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Alright, then where to next?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Where else?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Tell your new friends at Kazdel that the Lich King’s Court... No, not the court—tell them that the keepers of the Temple of Knowledge are preparing to return home.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The special correspondence with Ewigegnade is over. I shared Laterano's caution and, once again, offered my hopes of advancing together with Leithanien.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: When the time comes, we will further analyze the incident in Zwillingstürme according to the information brought back by Federico Giallo.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It was clearly more than just a revolt instigated by the remnants of the Witch King.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Perhaps what happened there was a harbinger of the Disaster, much like the warning Laterano received.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Ewigegnade, the only Empress of Leithanien with a voice now... The way she spoke was appropriate enough, and her attitude sufficiently ambiguous. I could even imagine her expressions.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: ...All within my expectations.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The Lateran Declaration didn't really receive any practical response after the Summit of Nations. From the furthest coastlines to the centrum, the Disaster remains a secret in many countries.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Faith unites Laterano, while division has always been an everlasting blight upon this great land. But if we wait until the Disaster connects all nations into one...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It will be too late.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: We already have a vague outline of what we're facing, but are we still unable to deduce its source?

a.text: Analysis complete. Threat level at maximum.
Disaster unknown. Path simulation failed.
Laterano... synchronized outbreak.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Laterano will accelerate the development of yet more emergency response mechanisms.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: ...I need to reconfirm the list of suitable personnel.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: That settles the formalities of the handover.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: In accordance with the bilateral agreement between Laterano and Leithanien, the Empresses' Voice and I will ensure that Arturia Giallo returns to Leithanien when necessary.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The aforementioned agreement has been confirmed.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Phew... that's it.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I guess this is goodbye for real.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Michael, feel free to come find me anytime, whether I'm in Laterano or on Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Huh? This is new, Herr Executor. What's with the human touch in your words today?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Human touch? A uselessly vague descriptor.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I just have... an intuition.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This incident has not yet been fully resolved. To be more precise, what we experienced was just the beginning.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You're here at last, Federico.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The Empress let you go, but that does not mean I can immediately take you away. The handover procedure was somewhat more tedious than planned.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Fine work, I assume.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You heard Herkunftshorn's final words within the chaos.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What exactly did he tell you?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Get in line; everyone wants to know. Nobles, scholars, Witch King's remains, Ewigegnade... They're all guessing what exactly Herkunftshorn's legacy will be.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Might? Power? Knowledge?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What do you think, Federico?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...All I saw was an enormous mass of shadows that didn't exist in reality.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Herkunftshorn's death twenty-three years ago is the only fact of the matter.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: No matter how many images he fabricated for himself, or how many words he spoke, they were all simply echoes of the past.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: He may have failed to conquer death, but did manage to carve all his emotions into the void itself.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: His complacency, frustration, loathing, regret... and his expectations.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: He said our genesis is also our end, and that our abilities are also our incompetence.

a.text: 'The invasion of chaos is inevitable.'
'The master of all existence will awaken.'

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: A difficult threat to decipher.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Perhaps this is somehow related to His Holiness's attitude. He was the one who entrusted me with the mission of bringing you back to Laterano.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Arturia, you said at the amphitheater that you never left Laterano of your own accord...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Mm-hm.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I freely admit the gaps in our laws, and that emotion may be a supplementary force we can use to help Laterano face this new threat. But it is undefinable, and bound to come with unknown risks.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Therefore, I will increase my vigilance over you in order to determine the subjective motivations and possible objective consequences of your actions.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: IE: I will shoot to kill if I find anything suspicious.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I am most grateful, Your Beatitude, for with your refined rationality, you are my most suitable executioner.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Alright, Federico. If you're not in a hurry to set off on your next journey, then take a good look at this sunset.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: This is the moment where Zwillingstürme reveals the pinnacle of its beauty. Such splendor is both fleeting and fragile. Soon, night will fall.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Do you still remember the question you once asked me?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Laterano seems to stand eternally white and flawless, shining with an everlasting radiance. So where is the first place to light up when the sun goes down?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Back then, I promised you that I would bring you to the highest point in Laterano for a look.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I know the answer.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I went to the top of the Basilica after I met with the Pope and received my sainthood.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Once night falls in the city, the streets to the right of the Tower of Revelations will be the first to light up.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I even looked into why that is the case.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The Lateran Office of Electrical Management has an integrated program for the city's public energy grid. The area I mentioned belongs to the district where the Tower of Revelations is located.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Alcide, the operator at the management office, is left-handed and has a mild case of obsessive-compulsive disorder. He starts from the leftmost switch on the control panel everyday.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The lights start from that street to the right of the Tower of Revelations, and then through the Notarial Hall and firearm workshops in Pagus Michaelion, to the Sunset Chapel in Pagus Saint Marcel, and then all the way to the chapel square.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: At night, the streetlights in Laterano illuminate in order—

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I should have expected as much. Your answer, as the most rational person I know, is also—

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: And they look just as nice as they were before.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I was going to tell you that I actually wasn't as frightened as you might have thought, back in that tiny room.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Even constant darkness and silence cannot obstruct the feelings between two people.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Of course, your findings aren't bad at all either.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: They reminded me that my question does indeed have a definite answer, somewhere out there.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The lights will turn on again. Even the halos on our heads have never gone out.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Light is a constant, while darkness is temporary.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: As for our emotions... Grief and joy may happen only in certain moments of our lives, but we can always feel them, all the time.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: They have never left us.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: ...Like how the sunset has never truly left this sky.
